skill.name: sast-bandit
skill.description: Guide Bandit SAST scans for Python projects, triage findings by severity and confidence, and map remediation to CWE and OWASP guidance.
skill.summary: Run and interpret Bandit security scans for Python code and CI workflows.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives from configuration lists, Markdown formatting, references, and labeled vulnerable examples. Confirmed risks include unsafe eval suppression, unvalidated subprocess guidance, fragile xargs filename handling, and unsafe pickle suppression. Third-party hooks and actions also use mutable references.

remediation.issue: The examples suppress Bandit warnings around eval and pickle deserialization.
remediation.suggestion: Remove these suppression examples. Use a structured parser, or enforce strict trusted-source and integrity controls when replacement is impossible.

remediation.issue: A safe-labeled subprocess example accepts an unvalidated filename.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve the path within an approved directory, reject traversal and option-like values, and prefer direct file APIs over cat.

remediation.issue: The changed-file pipeline passes repository filenames through unsafe xargs parsing.
remediation.suggestion: Use null-delimited filenames, terminate options explicitly, and reject paths that Bandit could interpret as command options.

remediation.issue: Remote hooks and actions use mutable version tags.
remediation.suggestion: Pin executable dependencies to reviewed commit hashes and use automated updates to keep those hashes current.

remediation.issue: The skill references scripts/bandit_analyzer.py, but the file is absent.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle and audit the script, or remove claims that depend on enhanced reporting and ticket creation.

content.value_statement: Python security flaws can reach production unnoticed. This skill guides Bandit scans, prioritization, CI integration, and remediation with CWE and OWASP references.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to run Bandit against Python files, directories, and configured projects.
Organizes findings by Bandit severity, confidence, location, and CWE reference.
Provides remediation examples for injection, cryptography, deserialization, TLS, XML, and template risks.
Supplies baseline Bandit and pre-commit configuration examples.
Guides CI security gates and progressive enforcement for legacy projects.
limitations: The referenced scripts/bandit_analyzer.py file is not included in this package.
Bandit cannot reliably detect business logic, authorization, or runtime flaws.
Results depend on the Bandit version, enabled tests, exclusions, and confidence thresholds.
Reports can expose source snippets or secrets unless code output and access are restricted.

use_cases.title: Triage a Python Feature
use_cases.description: Scan changed Python files, review high-confidence findings, and prepare focused fixes before code review.

use_cases.title: Establish an Application Baseline
use_cases.description: Inventory existing Bandit findings, map them to CWE and OWASP, and define remediation priorities.

use_cases.title: Add a CI Security Gate
use_cases.description: Configure Bandit or pre-commit checks that block selected severity levels while preserving reviewable reports.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan the Python files in [path] with Bandit. Use a read-only workflow, explain the command, and summarize findings by severity and confidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: First scan of a small Python project

prompt_templates.title: Review a Bandit Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the Bandit report at [path]. Prioritize exploitable findings, identify likely false positives, and recommend one verification step for each priority item.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Bandit gate for [repository]. Specify scan scope, thresholds, exclusions, report retention, failure behavior, and a safe exception review process.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze Bandit findings in [report]. Map each confirmed issue to CWE and OWASP, rank exploitability, propose fixes, and define validation tests.

output_examples.input: Review Bandit finding B602 in payments/tasks.py.
output: Priority: High because user input reaches a shell-enabled subprocess.
Recommended action: use a fixed executable with validated arguments and no shell.
Validation: test metacharacters, traversal values, and unexpected option-like inputs.

output_examples.input: Plan a Bandit gate for a legacy Python service.
output: Start by recording all findings without blocking builds.
Block new high-severity, high-confidence findings after the baseline is reviewed.
Store restricted reports and require documented approval for suppressions.

best_practices: Run scans with read-only source access and restrict report access.
Review exploitability before suppression, and document every accepted exception.
Pin Bandit, hooks, and CI actions to reviewed immutable versions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every Bandit finding as a confirmed vulnerability.
Do not suppress eval, pickle, or shell findings without a documented trust boundary.
Do not publish reports containing credentials or sensitive source snippets.

faq.question: Does this skill install Bandit automatically?
faq.answer: It provides installation commands and configurations. Confirm package installation and external downloads before execution.

faq.question: Which languages can Bandit scan?
faq.answer: Bandit analyzes Python source code. Use other tools for non-Python languages.

faq.question: Does Bandit cover the complete OWASP Top 10?
faq.answer: No. It covers selected Python patterns, while business logic and authorization issues require additional review.

faq.question: How should false positives be handled?
faq.answer: Verify data flow and exploitability first. Record a precise justification before adding a targeted suppression.

faq.question: Can Bandit reports contain secrets?
faq.answer: Yes. Reports may include source snippets, so restrict access or disable code excerpts.

faq.question: Is the enhanced analyzer included?
faq.answer: No. The package references scripts/bandit_analyzer.py, but that file is absent.
